samples.question: Three square plates are drawn side by side on white paper: a left plate, a centre plate and a right plate. Each plate is solid black except for the white corridors cut into it, and every plate is surrounded by a closed black rim. Inside one plate you may walk anywhere along the white corridors, but you may never step on black. A plate CONTAINS A ROUND TRIP when you can start somewhere in its white corridors, walk, and come back to your starting point without ever turning around and without walking back along any stretch of corridor you have already used; otherwise the plate is LOOP FREE. Short black spurs stick out from the walls into some corridors; a spur that stops short of the opposite wall leaves a gap you may walk through. Exactly one of the three plates is loop free, and the three plates carry exactly the same amount of black ink. Which plate is the loop-free one - left, centre or right?
